ok_bad_beta_podcast_studio.blurb: A dozen boulder problems in the Wichita Mountains of southwest Oklahoma, on an overhanging face and slab headwall at the eastern end of the Jug City boulder field. Grades run from VB-level problems up to the V7 range, with a hard core around V4 to V7, and the hardest lines are on the steep wall. Five of the main lines have very good landings, while falls beside them can be serious, so bring pads and spotters and watch the ground. The granite is featured and juggy. Getting in takes a walk from the lake loop, down across a creek and up through sumac on deer trails.

ok_little_willies_wonder_wall.blurb: A short granite wall on Mount Scott in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma, with one of the shortest walks in on the mountain. Twelve lines mix boulder problems, mostly V2 to V6 with one much harder outlier, and a handful of easy trad routes around 5.6 to 5.7. The rock is solid with good holds and incut crimps. The wall faces the afternoon and has tree shade in the morning, so it is a reasonable pick when the weather is warm. A short grassy slope leads to the base.

ok_shadowland.blurb: A gully of shady, north-facing cliffs in Charon's Gardens, in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma, between Nemo's and Icarus Cave. Eleven lines: mostly boulder problems from easy to roughly V6, plus a few trad routes, two of them at 5.11 and one at 5.12. Expect little in the way of freebies. There are highballs, and ledges with shorter problems above taller ones, though a few short problems sit at the base of the gully. The cool aspect suits warm days. The walk starts from the pull-out near the Steak Dinner boulder and leads up toward the gully.

ok_luxor.blurb: A single pyramid-shaped granite boulder near Mount Scott in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma, climbed on three faces so separate groups can share it. Eleven problems range from easy up to the V8 range, with most in the V2 to V3 band. Many are tall, around 15 to 18 feet, and the west face overhangs, so the style leans toward power and endurance. Two or three pads plus a spotter are wise; the traverse on the back makes a good warm-up, and the grades are loose. It sits a short walk up from a roadside pull-out.

ok_upstream_boulders.blurb: A scattering of granite boulders in Charon's Gardens, in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma, a few minutes beyond the Steak Dinner boulder. Eleven problems cover a wide spread, from easy lines through the V2 to V4 range up to a very hard V12 on the cave boulder. The best-known cluster is two boulders beside the stream, with other problems on a bluff near the mountain's base. A cave can be seen from the road. Trails here are faint and overgrown, so expect some bushwhacking from the road and use the cave and creek as landmarks.

ok_back_alley_the.blurb: A sub-area of the Roadside Boulders in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge of southwest Oklahoma, set back from the road with a view over the creek. Eleven granite problems run from an easy warm-up to V10, with most in the V1 to V3 range, so it works for a mixed group. The stone is solid, though the Roadside Boulders in general can be sharp on the skin. It sits roughly 200 feet behind the Darkstar Boulder, itself only a couple of minutes on foot up the road from the first pull-off.

ok_troop_wall.blurb: A short, slightly less than vertical wall in the Autobahn area of Chandler Park near Tulsa, Oklahoma, good for both bouldering and top-roping. Ten lines include easy traverses and problems, a few mid-range ones, and a couple of hard V7-level lines, plus two top-rope routes in the 5.6 to 5.9 range. The rock is high quality and the wall gets some sun. It is a recommended spot for first-time climbers and can fill up with top-ropers. Look for the scratched troop number and year at waist height, directly opposite Disease Wall.
